original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descending-properties}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of schemes.
Let $\tau \in \{fpqc, \linebreak[0] fppf, \linebreak[0]
\etale, \linebreak[0] smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic\}$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the property is local in the Zariski topology,
\item for any morphism of affine schemes $S' \to S$
which is flat, flat of finite presentation,
\'etale, smooth or syntomic depending on whether $\tau$ is
fpqc, fppf, \'etale, smooth, or syntomic,
property $\mathcal{P}$ holds for $S'$ if property $\mathcal{P}$
holds for $S$, and
\item for any surjective morphism of affine schemes $S' \to S$
which is flat, flat of finite presentation,
\'etale, smooth or syntomic depending on whether $\tau$ is
fpqc, fppf, \'etale, smooth, or syntomic,
property $\mathcal{P}$ holds for $S$ if property $\mathcal{P}$
holds for $S'$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{P}$ is $\tau$ local on the base.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $\mathcal P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of schemes and choose $\tau$ among fpqc, fppf, étale, smooth, and syntomic. A property is *local for the $\tau$-topology* if for every $\tau$-covering $\{S_i\to S\}$ it holds on $S$ if and only if it holds on every $S_i$. Suppose (1) $\mathcal P$ is Zariski-local; (2) for every affine morphism $S'\to S$ which is flat (for fpqc), flat of finite presentation (for fppf), étale (for étale), smooth (for smooth), or syntomic (for syntomic), $\mathcal P$ ascends from $S$ to $S'$; and (3) for every surjective affine morphism in the corresponding class, $\mathcal P$ descends from $S'$ to $S$. Then $\mathcal P$ is local for the $\tau$-topology.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves the three descent criteria for a Zariski-local property P of schemes: stability under admissible affine flat/fppf/étale/smooth/syntomic morphisms, reflection along admissible surjective affine morphisms, concluding P is local for the chosen topology.

hypotheses: P is Zariski-local, ascends through indicated affine tau morphisms, and descends through surjective ones.
conclusions: P can be checked on arbitrary tau coverings.
